topic: Adaptive Multi-Agent Orchestration with Runtime Topology Switching

papers.title: AdaptOrch: Task-Adaptive Multi-Agent Orchestration in the Era of LLM Performance Convergence
papers.contribution: Presents a formal framework for task-adaptive multi-agent orchestration that dynamically selects among four canonical topologies (parallel, sequential, hierarchical, debate). Argues that orchestration topology dominates system-level performance when underlying LLM capabilities converge.
papers.limitation: Selects topology per-task at dispatch time rather than switching mid-execution. Does not use execution trace features for online adaptation. Static assignment based on task metadata.

papers.title: DyTopo: Dynamic Topology Routing for Multi-Agent Reasoning via Semantic Matching
papers.contribution: Introduces a manager-guided multi-agent framework that dynamically reconstructs sparse directed communication topologies each reasoning round using semantic matching between agent outputs.
papers.limitation: Routing decisions based on semantic similarity rather than task-structure estimation. Evaluated only on reasoning benchmarks, not on heterogeneous agentic tasks with tool use.

papers.title: MAS-on-the-Fly: Dynamic Adaptation of LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems at Test Time
papers.contribution: Proposes MASFly, a framework enabling dynamic adaptation of multi-agent systems at test time without extra training, inspired by biological adaptation. Uses retrieval-based mechanism for agent role adaptation.
papers.limitation: Adapts agent roles and retrieval strategies rather than switching between structurally different topologies. No formalization of task-structure dimensions.

papers.title: Multi-Agent Collaboration via Evolving Orchestration
papers.contribution: Proposes a puppeteer-style paradigm where a centralized orchestrator trained via reinforcement learning dynamically sequences and prioritizes agents. The orchestrator learns to adaptively route tasks to specialist agents.
papers.limitation: RL-trained orchestrator learns a fixed policy; does not explicitly model task-structure dimensions or support mid-task topology switching between structurally different architectures.

papers.title: Multi-Agent Design: Optimizing Agents with Better Prompts and Topologies (MASS)
papers.contribution: Proposes MASS (Multi-Agent System Search), a three-stage optimization framework that jointly optimizes prompts and communication topologies for multi-agent systems. First to systematically search over topology space.
papers.limitation: Offline optimization at design time. The found topology is static once deployed; no runtime switching based on execution signals.

papers.title: G-Designer: Architecting Multi-Agent Communication Topologies via Graph Neural Networks
papers.contribution: First to use graph neural networks for designing task-aware multi-agent communication topologies. Uses a variational graph auto-encoder to model agent networks and dynamically generate communication graphs.
papers.limitation: Generates topology per-task at dispatch; no mid-execution adaptation. Communication graph is fixed once generated for a given task.

papers.title: AFlow: Automating Agentic Workflow Generation
papers.contribution: Automates workflow generation through Monte Carlo Tree Search over code-represented workflow nodes and edges. Outperforms hand-designed pipelines by 5.7% across multiple benchmarks.
papers.limitation: Searches workflow space offline at design time. Generated workflows are static during execution. Relies on predefined operators.

papers.title: A2Flow: Automating Agentic Workflow Generation via Self-Adaptive Operators
papers.contribution: Extends AFlow by introducing self-adaptive operators that can modify workflow structure during search. Removes dependency on predefined operator templates.
papers.limitation: Still an offline search procedure. Does not adapt workflows at runtime based on execution feedback.

papers.title: EvoFlow: Evolving Diverse Agentic Workflows On The Fly
papers.contribution: Uses niching evolutionary algorithms to automatically search a population of heterogeneous and complexity-adaptive agentic workflows. Maintains diversity in the workflow population.
papers.limitation: Evolutionary search is an offline procedure despite the 'on the fly' framing. Population evolves across tasks, not within a single task execution.

papers.title: Automated Design of Agentic Systems (ADAS)
papers.contribution: Introduces the ADAS research area and Meta Agent Search algorithm, where a meta-agent iteratively programs and improves new agent designs. Demonstrates that learned agents outperform hand-designed ones.
papers.limitation: Meta-agent search is offline. Discovered agent designs are fixed at deployment. No runtime switching mechanism.

papers.title: AgentSquare: Automatic LLM Agent Search in Modular Design Space
papers.contribution: Proposes modular LLM agent search (MoLAS) with four fundamental modules (Planning, Reasoning, Tool-Use, Memory). Uses module evolution and recombination to search agent designs.
papers.limitation: Module-level search is offline. Does not address runtime topology switching or task-structure estimation.

papers.title: GPTSwarm: Language Agents as Optimizable Graphs
papers.contribution: Unifies LLM-based agents as computational graphs where nodes are operations and edges define information flow. Provides automatic graph optimizers for both node-level prompt refinement and graph connectivity optimization.
papers.limitation: Graph optimization is performed offline. Does not dynamically switch graph structure during task execution based on runtime signals.

papers.title: MDAgents: An Adaptive Collaboration of LLMs for Medical Decision-Making
papers.contribution: Automatically assigns collaboration structure (solo vs. group) based on medical task complexity. Adapts between single-agent and multi-agent configurations, emulating real clinical decision-making workflows.
papers.limitation: Binary adaptation (solo vs. group) in medical domain only. Does not support fine-grained topology switching or task-structure estimation from execution traces.

papers.title: DyLAN: A Dynamic LLM-Powered Agent Network for Task-Oriented Agent Collaboration
papers.contribution: Proposes dynamic agent team selection and adaptive communication structures. Agents are selected from a candidate pool and communicate through dynamically constructed networks based on task requirements.
papers.limitation: Team composition is selected per-task at dispatch time. Communication structure does not change during execution. Up to 25% accuracy improvement on MMLU subsets.

papers.title: AgentVerse: Facilitating Multi-Agent Collaboration and Exploring Emergent Behaviors
papers.contribution: Simulates human group problem-solving processes to enhance multi-agent collaboration. Supports dynamic adjustment of agent group composition through recruitment, communication, and decision-making stages.
papers.limitation: Group dynamics follow predefined stage patterns. Does not formalize task structure or enable runtime topology switching between fundamentally different orchestration architectures.

papers.title: AutoAgents: A Framework for Automatic Agent Generation
papers.contribution: Adaptively generates and coordinates multiple specialized agents tailored to input tasks. Automatically determines agent roles and collaboration patterns.
papers.limitation: Agent generation is a one-time setup per task. Does not re-generate or switch agent configurations during execution based on intermediate results.

papers.title: AgentNet: Decentralized Evolutionary Coordination for LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
papers.contribution: Proposes decentralized RAG-based framework enabling LLM agents to specialize, evolve, and collaborate without a central orchestrator. Eliminates single points of failure in multi-agent coordination.
papers.limitation: Decentralized evolution is slow and does not support rapid topology switching within a single task execution.

papers.title: MetaAgent: Automatically Constructing Multi-Agent Systems Based on Finite State Machines
papers.contribution: Uses finite state machines to automatically generate multi-agent systems from task descriptions. FSM structure allows predefined state transitions but supports LLM-driven decision-making at transition points.
papers.limitation: FSM structure is fixed after generation. State transitions are predefined, not learned from execution traces. Does not support topology switching.

papers.title: Dr. MAS: Stable Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Agent LLM Systems
papers.contribution: Provides an end-to-end RL training framework for multi-agent LLM systems with stable optimization. Supports scalable orchestration and flexible per-agent LLM serving.
papers.limitation: Trains a fixed orchestration policy via RL. Does not support runtime topology switching or task-structure-aware adaptation.

papers.title: DIG to Heal: Scaling General-purpose Agent Collaboration via Explainable Dynamic Decision Paths
papers.contribution: Introduces Dynamic Interaction Graphs (DIG) that capture emergent collaboration as time-evolving causal networks of agent activations. Makes collaboration dynamics observable and explainable.
papers.limitation: Focuses on diagnosing and healing collaboration failures rather than proactively switching topologies. Post-hoc analysis rather than predictive adaptation.

papers.title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail? (MAST)
papers.contribution: Presents MAST (Multi-Agent Systems Failure Taxonomy) built from analysis of 150+ execution traces across 7 frameworks. Identifies 14 unique failure modes with grounded theory methodology.
papers.limitation: Purely diagnostic: taxonomizes failures post-hoc but does not propose runtime intervention or topology switching to prevent failures.

papers.title: TraceCoder: A Trace-Driven Multi-Agent Framework for Automated Debugging
papers.contribution: Introduces trace-driven debugging where execution traces guide a multi-agent framework through observe-analyze-repair cycles. Demonstrates that execution trace features can drive agent behavior adaptation.
papers.limitation: Trace analysis is specific to code debugging. Does not generalize to arbitrary task-structure estimation or topology switching.

papers.title: RouteLLM: Learning to Route LLMs with Preference Data
papers.contribution: Develops a training framework for router models that dynamically select between a stronger and weaker LLM based on query characteristics. Reduces costs by 2x while maintaining quality.
papers.limitation: Routes between two individual models, not between multi-agent topologies. Does not consider task-structure dimensions.

papers.title: Learning to Route LLMs from Bandit Feedback
papers.contribution: Formulates LLM routing as a contextual bandit problem. Develops bandit-based algorithm supporting preference-tunable routing with online learning from feedback.
papers.limitation: Routes between individual LLMs, not topologies. Bandit feedback is per-query, not per-execution-step within a task.

papers.title: Neural Bandit Based Optimal LLM Selection for a Pipeline of Tasks
papers.contribution: Uses neural network-based contextual bandit for optimal LLM selection across a pipeline of subtasks. First to address sequential multi-step LLM selection.
papers.limitation: Selects LLM models, not orchestration topologies. Does not consider structural task properties or mid-pipeline topology switching.

papers.title: MultiAgentBench: Evaluating the Collaboration and Competition of LLM Agents
papers.contribution: Comprehensive benchmark evaluating LLM-based multi-agent systems across diverse interactive scenarios including both cooperation and competition. Evaluates multiple organizational structures.
papers.limitation: Evaluates fixed organizational structures per scenario. Does not test adaptive or runtime-switching approaches.

papers.title: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents
papers.contribution: Establishes multi-dimensional evaluation across 8 environments for LLM agents. Reveals large capability gaps between commercial and open-source models.
papers.limitation: Evaluates single-agent configurations only. Does not assess multi-agent topologies.

papers.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
papers.contribution: Provides 2,294 real-world GitHub issue resolution tasks with Docker-isolated execution. Gold standard for evaluating code generation agents.
papers.limitation: Evaluates code generation quality but not the effect of orchestration topology choices on task success.

papers.title: WebArena: A Realistic Web Environment for Building Autonomous Agents
papers.contribution: Offers 812 long-horizon web navigation tasks in realistic self-hosted environments. Best GPT-4 agent achieves 14.41% vs 78.24% human performance.
papers.limitation: Designed for single-agent evaluation. No multi-agent topology comparison.

papers.title: GAIA: A Benchmark for General AI Assistants
papers.contribution: Tests fundamental assistant abilities with 466 questions. GPT-4 with plugins scored 15% versus 92% for humans, highlighting the gap in general assistance.
papers.limitation: Single-agent evaluation framework. Does not compare orchestration strategies.

papers.title: AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation
papers.contribution: Pioneered conversation-based multi-agent orchestration where agents coordinate through multi-turn dialogue. Supports flexible conversation patterns and human-in-the-loop.
papers.limitation: Single topology (conversation-based). No mechanism to switch to hierarchical or DAG-based execution when conversation topology is suboptimal.

papers.title: MetaGPT: Meta Programming for A Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework
papers.contribution: Encodes Standardized Operating Procedures into a sequential pipeline with verification gates. Achieves 85.9% Pass@1 on code generation through role-specialized agents.
papers.limitation: Fixed hierarchical SOP topology. Cannot adapt to tasks that would benefit from flat conversation or debate.

papers.title: CAMEL: Communicative Agents for 'Mind' Exploration of Large Language Model Society
papers.contribution: Introduced inception prompting for role-playing agents and generated 25,000+ cooperative dialogues. Established the role-playing topology as a distinct orchestration pattern.
papers.limitation: Fixed role-playing topology. Does not support switching to hierarchical or DAG-based patterns.

papers.title: ChatDev: Communicative Agents for Software Development
papers.contribution: Extended role-playing into a virtual software company with chat-chain orchestration. Demonstrated that structured role assignment improves software generation quality.
papers.limitation: Chat-chain topology is fixed. Cannot adapt when debugging phases would benefit from different coordination patterns than design phases.

papers.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that intermediate reasoning steps significantly improve LLM performance on arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic reasoning tasks. Foundational technique for agent reasoning.
papers.limitation: Single-agent prompting technique. Does not address multi-agent coordination.

papers.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
papers.contribution: Proposes interleaving reasoning traces and task-specific actions for grounded decision-making via external tool interaction.
papers.limitation: Single-agent framework. Does not address multi-agent topology decisions.

papers.title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Extends chain-of-thought into branching exploration. Improved Game of 24 from 4% to 74% through deliberate tree search over thought steps.
papers.limitation: Single-agent deliberation. The branching strategy is fixed, not adaptive to task structure.

papers.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: Reinforces language agents through linguistic feedback rather than weight updates. Stores reflections in episodic memory for self-improvement across trials.
papers.limitation: Single-agent self-improvement loop. Does not coordinate multiple agents or adapt orchestration structure.

papers.title: Plan-and-Act: Improving Planning of Agents for Long-Horizon Tasks
papers.contribution: Separates planner from executor, achieving 57.58% on WebArena-Lite. Demonstrates that explicit planning improves long-horizon task completion.
papers.limitation: Fixed plan-then-execute architecture. Does not adapt planning strategy based on execution feedback.

papers.title: DyFlow: Dynamic Workflow Framework for Agentic Reasoning
papers.contribution: Proposes feedback-driven framework for LLM agents that dynamically adapts subgoal planning based on execution feedback. Demonstrates that dynamic workflow modification improves task completion.
papers.limitation: Adapts subgoal plans within a single workflow pattern. Does not switch between structurally different topologies.

papers.title: Improving Factuality and Reasoning in Language Models through Multiagent Debate
papers.contribution: Shows that multiple LLM instances debating over rounds improves factual accuracy and mathematical reasoning. Establishes debate as a canonical multi-agent topology.
papers.limitation: Only evaluates debate topology. Does not compare against hierarchical or other structural alternatives.

papers.title: ReConcile: Round-Table Conference Improves Reasoning via Consensus among Diverse LLMs
papers.contribution: Enhanced multi-agent debate with confidence-weighted voting, surpassing baselines by up to 11.4%. Showed that diverse LLMs in a round-table format improve consensus quality.
papers.limitation: Evaluates one specific debate variant. Fixed topology throughout execution.

papers.title: Debate Does Not Help Humans Fact-Check LLM-Generated News Articles
papers.contribution: Found that most debate frameworks do not consistently outperform chain-of-thought or self-consistency baselines. Important negative result showing topology choice matters.
papers.limitation: Only compares within debate-style topologies. Does not evaluate when switching from debate to hierarchical would help.

papers.title: Team of Thoughts: Efficient Test-time Scaling of Agentic Multi-Agent Systems
papers.contribution: Enables multiple specialized LLMs to collaborate via tool-calling interfaces without redundant computation. Demonstrates efficient test-time scaling for agentic multi-agent systems.
papers.limitation: Fixed collaboration pattern. Does not adapt topology based on task-structure analysis.

papers.title: On-Policy Reinforcement Learning for Collaborative LLMs
papers.contribution: Trains LLMs as agents that propose and revise answers through shared discussion and debate using on-policy RL. Demonstrates MARL-based training for multi-agent LLM collaboration.
papers.limitation: Trains a fixed collaboration protocol. Does not support runtime switching between collaboration modes.

papers.title: MAGE: Meta-Reinforcement Learning for Language Agents toward Generalizable Collaboration
papers.contribution: Applies meta-RL to LLM agents for generalizable multi-agent collaboration. Agents learn to adapt collaboration strategies across tasks through meta-learning.
papers.limitation: Focuses on single-agent exploration induced by meta-RL. Does not address topology-level switching or task-structure estimation.

papers.title: Plan-and-Act: Separating Planning from Execution for LLM Agents
papers.contribution: Separates planner from executor, achieving 57.58% on WebArena-Lite. Establishes that plan-execute separation improves long-horizon task success.
papers.limitation: Static separation. Planner does not switch execution strategies based on runtime signals.

papers.title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that LLMs can self-learn API invocation patterns. Foundational for tool-use in agentic systems.
papers.limitation: Single-agent tool learning. Does not address how multiple agents coordinate shared tool access.

papers.title: ToolLLM: Facilitating Large Language Models to Master 16000+ Real-World APIs
papers.contribution: Scales tool use to 16,464 real-world APIs. Provides infrastructure for multi-tool agent evaluation.
papers.limitation: Single-agent framework. Does not consider orchestration topology effects on tool-use coordination.

papers.title: Test-Time Adaptation for LLM Agents via Environment Simulation
papers.contribution: Uses world model predictions to help agents reason about next states on-the-fly. Demonstrates test-time adaptation through environment simulation.
papers.limitation: Adapts single-agent behavior, not multi-agent topology. Environment model is separate from task-structure estimation.

papers.title: A Survey on LLM-based Autonomous Agents
papers.contribution: Comprehensive survey proposing a unified agent framework covering perception, brain (reasoning/planning), and action modules. Catalogs coordination patterns without experimental comparison.
papers.limitation: Survey only; no experimental cross-topology comparison. Notes the gap without addressing it.

papers.title: A Survey on Evaluation of LLM-based Agents
papers.contribution: Explicitly flags orchestration evaluation as underexplored. Catalogs existing evaluation approaches and identifies the lack of topology-aware benchmarks.
papers.limitation: Identifies the problem but does not propose solutions or experimental methodology for topology evaluation.

papers.title: Integrated Adaptive Communication in Multi-Agent Systems: Dynamic Topology, Frequency, and Content Optimization
papers.contribution: Proposes integrated optimization of communication topology, frequency, and content in multi-agent systems. Shows that joint optimization outperforms optimizing each dimension independently.
papers.limitation: Classical multi-agent systems, not LLM-based. Communication topology changes are continuous, not discrete switches between named topologies.

papers.title: Decentralized Adaptive Task Allocation for Dynamic Multi-Agent Systems
papers.contribution: Presents a decentralized two-layer architecture for dynamic task assignment in multi-agent systems under partial observability. Demonstrates effective runtime task reallocation.
papers.limitation: Classical MAS setting, not LLM-based. Task allocation rather than topology switching.

papers.title: Dynamic Generation of Multi-LLM Agent Communication Topologies with Graph Diffusion Models
papers.contribution: Uses graph diffusion models to dynamically generate communication topologies for multi-LLM agent systems. Generates diverse topological structures through learned diffusion process.
papers.limitation: Generative model produces topology at dispatch time. Does not switch topology during execution.

papers.title: AgentRx: Systematic Debugging for AI Agents
papers.contribution: Treats agent execution like a system trace that needs validation. Uses structured trace analysis to diagnose agent failures systematically rather than relying on a single LLM judge.
papers.limitation: Diagnostic tool for post-hoc debugging. Does not use trace signals for runtime topology adaptation.

papers.title: BEST-Route: Adaptive LLM Routing with Test-Time Optimal Compute
papers.contribution: Optimally balances cost and quality through multi-armed bandit routing at test time. Demonstrates that adaptive routing outperforms fixed model assignment.
papers.limitation: Routes between models, not between orchestration topologies. Does not consider task-structure dimensions.

papers.title: LLM Bandit: Cost-Efficient LLM Generation via Preference-Based Multi-Armed Bandits
papers.contribution: Formulates LLM selection as a multi-armed bandit problem enabling dynamic and intelligent routing of queries. Demonstrates cost reduction while maintaining quality.
papers.limitation: Bandit operates at query level, not at topology level. No concept of task phases or structural transitions.

clusters.name: adaptive-orchestration

clusters.name: dynamic-composition

clusters.name: execution-analysis
clusters.description: Methods for analyzing agent execution traces, diagnosing failures, and understanding collaboration dynamics.

clusters.name: rl-orchestration
clusters.description: Reinforcement learning approaches for training orchestration policies in multi-agent LLM systems.

clusters.name: tool-use
clusters.description: Foundational work on LLM tool use and API integration.

clusters.description: Surveys and meta-analyses of LLM agent and multi-agent systems.
